title: Rate Cloud: frequently asked questions
excerpt: Product information reflects the official website on November 3, 2026. Check the live dashboard and terms before purchasing.
text: Product information reflects the official website on November 3, 2026. Check the live dashboard and terms before purchasing. What is Rate Cloud? Rate Cloud provides subscription API access to GLM, DeepSeek, and Qwen for development, AI agents, automation, and applications. A subscription selects a model and an access period rather than billing each million tokens. See the service overview . Is there a token limit? There is no cumulative input or output token quota during an active subscription. A single operation still has finite context capacity, a deadline, and technical constraints. Actual processing volume depends on speed, input and output lengths, available slots, and service availability. Does four slots mean only four requests? No. A paid subscription allows four requests to run at the same time. Completed requests free their slots for new work. Several API keys on the same account use the relevant model's shared slot pool. Can I add more parallel capacity? The public offer allows combining subscriptions. Two subscriptions to the same model provide eight slots for that model. Different model subscriptions provide their own model-specific pools. Which models can I use? The published catalog lists GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Qwen 3.8 Max. See the dated catalog for exact API IDs, prices, positioning, and image-input support. Is a Flash model the same as a Pro model? No. They are distinct catalog entries. Precision profiles are execution variants of the selected model; they are not permission to substitute another model silently. See routing and quantization . How does intelligent routing choose a precision profile? The published design checks task requirements and eligible replicas, prioritizes quality for difficult or uncertain work, and considers cost only among suitable routes. Context, images, tools, output format, available memory, queues, and replica health influence eligibility. Profile support depends on the specific model and hardware. Does quantization guarantee identical answers? No. Numerical precision can affect output quality. The public architecture describes validation against the source release and task-specific quality gates. An economical profile is eligible only where its quality is suitable. Quantization is separate from reasoning-effort settings. Which applications can connect? The official guide covers OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Continue, Hermes, and other compatible clients. Our practical guides cover selected setups. Client and model support determine available features; connecting a client does not change the selected model into a first-party model from the client's vendor. What base URL should my application use? The general OpenAI-compatible base URL is https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 . Dedicated compatibility URLs exist for particular clients. Use the official documentation and the matching guide rather than mixing endpoint families. Why can a listed model reject my request? Catalog visibility does not establish execution access. Check an active trial or subscription, key model permissions, expiry, IP restrictions, and client compatibility settings. Also check occupied slots and the returned error. Share the time and request identifier with support without sending the key or private content. How fast is Rate Cloud? The website publishes a historical performance table. It measures complete-request latency and effective token rates including waiting. Your task can differ. See performance and methodology ; the figures are not a guaranteed SLA or controlled identical-prompt benchmark. Are prompts used to train models? The service states that user data is not used to train models and that no permanent prompt-and-response text history is created. Temporary processing, isolated computational cache, operational metadata, and account records are separate categories. See privacy and reliability and the current privacy policy linked from the website. Is every model guaranteed to be available 24/7? No. The site expressly does not guarantee continuous availability of every model. The published compensation rule covers a specific complete system outage condition, not every slow request or individual model error. Consult the applicable terms. Can I test before paying? The published introductory trial provides the first three hours with one concurrent slot after registration and email and Telegram verification. Confirm your trial status in the dashboard. Can I sell subscriptions under my own brand? Rate Cloud offers White Label services with branding, a site and dashboard, payments, and technical infrastructure. See the White Label article and current official offer . Sources: homepage , how it works , and API guide . Does Rate Cloud operate the models itself? The published operating model covers leasing enterprise compute, placing model weights, and operating inference engines, replicas, precision profiles, and routing. See our infrastructure for the hardware families and operational responsibilities. This describes the public architecture, not an exclusive-path guarantee for every request. What does the referral program offer? A valid invitation for a new account provides five trial hours instead of three and 10% off the first subscription purchase, subject to verification and eligibility rules. The referrer can receive 10%, 3%, and 1% from qualifying payments along the three-step recommendation chain. Read referral details for attribution, payment exclusions, pending periods, and withdrawal rules. Register for the standard trial after checking the current terms. Email and Telegram verification are required and the standard trial uses one concurrent slot. If invited, use the actual personal invitation before registration. White Label has separate partner terms.

title: What Rate Cloud offers
excerpt: Rate Cloud is built around a simple purchasing model: pay for access to a selected AI model for a defined period, then use its API without a cumulative token allowance. This is particularly usefu
text: Rate Cloud is built around a simple purchasing model: pay for access to a selected AI model for a defined period, then use its API without a cumulative token allowance. This is particularly useful when an application makes many model calls and a token-based bill becomes hard to predict. An autonomous coding agent can read a repository, plan a change, edit files, run tools, inspect errors, and repeat the process many times. Each cycle can involve another request and additional input and output tokens. Rate Cloud's subscription price does not increase with the number of tokens consumed during the active subscription. Unlimited tokens and finite processing capacity Unlimited tokens means Rate Cloud does not impose a daily, weekly, or monthly quota on the total input and output tokens used during the paid period. It does not mean a single request can contain an unlimited context or run forever. Context capacity, operation deadlines, concurrent execution, protective limits, hardware capacity, and service availability remain finite. Actual monthly processing volume depends on the model, input length, output length, response speed, and available parallelism. Examples involving hundreds of millions or billions of tokens illustrate the pricing principle; they are not a promised monthly processing volume. Four concurrent slots per paid subscription Each paid subscription supplies four concurrent requests for its model. A slot represents one request currently being processed. Once that operation finishes, the slot becomes available again. It is not a limit of four requests per day or month. A developer might use all four slots for a main agent and three subagents, four separate work sessions, or independent automation jobs. API keys belonging to the same account share the relevant model's slot pool. Creating additional keys does not create additional capacity. Subscriptions can be combined. Two subscriptions to the same model provide eight slots for that model. Subscriptions to two different models provide separate pools: for example, four GLM slots and four DeepSeek slots. A workflow must send its requests to the appropriate model to use those pools. Access periods and getting started The website offers 3-, 7-, and 30-day subscriptions. New users can test the models during the first three hours after registration and the required email and Telegram verification, with one concurrent slot. Trial access and paid subscriptions have different allowances. Start with a representative task: a repository you actually work on, a typical document, or a real automation pattern. Evaluate the answer, tool behavior, and complete time to a usable result before choosing a model and subscription period. Where the service fits Rate Cloud can serve as the model layer behind coding agents, internal assistants, bots, data extraction pipelines, document workflows, and custom products. A compatible client provides its own interface, tools, project instructions, and history. The selected model and API integration determine which model-dependent features work. The service sells API access. Connecting a familiar application does not turn the selected GLM, DeepSeek, or Qwen model into that application's first-party model. Sources: Rate Cloud homepage and how it works . Snapshot: November 3, 2026. Back to overview .

title: How intelligent routing and quantization work
excerpt: Rate Cloud's public architecture describes a combination of stable compute capacity, additional available enterprise capacity, approved model precision profiles, and request-aware routing. The ob
text: Rate Cloud's public architecture describes a combination of stable compute capacity, additional available enterprise capacity, approved model precision profiles, and request-aware routing. The objective is to use resources efficiently while preserving the identity and functional requirements of the selected model. This article explains the published architecture. It is not an independent verification of every production deployment or a promise that every hardware and precision combination is always available. Compute capacity and model replicas The service describes renting spare capacity from enterprise cluster owners alongside a stable reserve. Rate Cloud manages model-weight placement, inference engines, precision profiles, and request distribution. The architecture names Huawei Atlas systems and Ascend accelerators, including Atlas 800I A2 and A3 for large models and Atlas 900 A2 PoD and A3 SuperPoD for distributed groups. Hardware compatibility is evaluated for each model. Moving a request between sites differs from splitting tightly coupled model computation across arbitrary sites: a replica's tightly coupled computation uses a compatible local network. A usable replica needs more than available memory. It must have compatible weights, runtime support, required API features, loaded state, warmup, and a successful readiness check. What quantization changes Model parameters and intermediate calculations can use different numerical formats. More compact formats reduce memory requirements and can change execution efficiency, but they can also affect output quality. Lower precision therefore needs evaluation against the relevant source release and task types. The published design uses quality, balanced, and economical profiles of the same model. A quality profile can use the validated original format, W8A8, or another approved configuration. A balanced profile can combine components at different precisions, such as 4 and 8 bits. An effective average near 6 bits does not imply a universal INT6 implementation. Economical profiles can use validated W4A16, W4A8, or MXFP4 configurations when the model and hardware support them. The availability of a named format depends on the model release, hardware, runtime, and quality checks. It is not a format offered indiscriminately for every model. Increasing the nominal precision of already quantized weights does not restore information lost during earlier quantization. Quality gates before routing Profiles are evaluated against the exact source model release on public, synthetic, and purpose-built tasks covering code, mathematics, long context, tools, and strict JSON. The published process considers answer quality, memory consumption, speed, and API behavior. User conversations are not used for model training or calibration. A compact profile is eligible only for tasks it can handle adequately. Difficult code, mathematics, tool workflows, strict schemas, and uncertain requests prioritize quality. A short prompt can still describe a difficult problem. Changing reasoning_effort is a separate control and should not be presented as an effect of quantization. How the router chooses The router considers context requirements, image inputs, tools, output format, task complexity, available memory, queue state, replica health, and the remaining resource allocation period. It first determines suitable routes; cost is considered among those suitable options. The selected model remains fixed. The operation also fixes the applicable weight revision and allowed features. An incompatible server is excluded before assignment. If suitable capacity is unavailable, the system can wait within its internal budget or return an explicit temporary-unavailability error rather than silently substituting another model. The request lifecycle Establish the protected connection and validate the API key, subscription, and available slot. Determine the request's requirements and choose an eligible profile of the requested model. Assign a ready, compatible replica and begin execution. Deliver the response, release the slot, and clear temporary content under the data-handling rules. A logical operation has a request_id ; individual compute attempts have an attempt_id . Before output begins, recovery may retry on a compatible replica within the original overall deadline. Recovery can increase latency. Once streaming has begun, the prefix of one generation must not be joined to a new generation's continuation. A broken stream is incomplete and must be handled as such by the client. Stable and interruptible resources Stable groups support the baseline workload and recovery. Additional interruptible groups expand capacity. A replica receiving a resource-revocation warning stops taking new operations. Losing a critical accelerator makes its dependent replica unavailable. Independent failure groups reduce the impact of a single fault, but recovery design does not guarantee every model is continuously available. Source: Rate Cloud: how it works , retrieved November 3, 2026. Back to overview .

title: Understanding Rate Cloud speed and performance

text: The useful performance question is how long it takes to receive a usable result for your workload. A high token rate during generation alone does not describe the complete experience: waiting, input processing, output length, and recovery all contribute. Published performance snapshot The following values were displayed on the Rate Cloud homepage on November 3, 2026. The date is the retrieval date, not an independently established measurement window. Model Typical complete response, seconds Typical effective tokens/second, including waiting Fast-response effective tokens/second, including waiting GLM 5.3 21.48 14.05 58.47 GLM 5.3 Flash 23.32 14.58 61.92 DeepSeek V4 Pro 15.67 25.83 127.84 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 14.99 19.22 78.38 Qwen 3.8 Max 21.37 13.13 80.68 These are published service observations, not guaranteed response times, fixed hardware benchmarks, or a controlled comparison on identical prompts. The homepage does not supply a cohort size or full measurement interval alongside this table, so the figures should not be treated as proof of sustained availability or an SLA. What the columns mean Complete response time runs from sending the request to receiving the finished result. It includes waiting, processing the input, and producing the answer. The website describes “typical” as the midpoint of the results: half are faster and half are slower. The effective token-rate figures include the whole request and its waiting time. They should not be relabeled as pure decode speed or time to first token. The fast-response column describes the fastest ten requests out of a hundred. It shows the faster end of the observed distribution, without promising that rate for a new request. Do not derive an average output length by multiplying independently summarized latency and throughput values. Why your task can take longer A long document requires more input processing than a brief question. A detailed answer takes longer to generate than a short one. Tool-driven agents may require multiple calls to finish one user task. Current load, profile eligibility, replica readiness, and recovery can also affect elapsed time. A model advertised for frequent or fast workloads can have a higher observed median response duration than another model when the observed request mixes differ. The table alone does not isolate model speed from prompt complexity, answer length, or user behavior. Concurrency and total throughput Four paid slots allow independent operations to progress at the same time. They do not make an individual request four times faster. Parallelism helps when the work can be split into independent tasks; a sequential reasoning or tool chain still waits for its dependencies. For a practical evaluation, measure your own time to a useful result, output correctness, incomplete requests, errors, and the proportion of tasks requiring retries. Record the model, input size, output size, concurrency, and observation period so results remain interpretable. Source: Rate Cloud's published performance table and explanations . text: Rate Cloud offers an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API and dedicated compatibility endpoints for supported coding clients. The official dashboard supplies application-specific setup instructions. Use those instructions for the installed client version and operating system. Published endpoints Purpose Endpoint OpenAI-compatible base URL https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 Model catalog GET https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/models Chat completions POST https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/chat/completions Responses POST https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/responses Codex compatibility base URL https://llm.rate-cloud.com/codex/v1 Claude Code compatibility base URL https://llm.rate-cloud.com/claude Direct /v1 requests authenticate with a bearer API key. Use an exact model ID from the catalog , such as glm-5.3 . Do not add the client-specific ratecloud/ prefix to a direct HTTP model identifier. From registration to the first request Register or sign in through Rate Cloud . Complete the verification needed for trial access or purchase access to the model you need. In the dashboard's API-key settings, create a named key, choose its model access, permitted IP addresses, and expiry, then copy the displayed secret immediately. A subscription provides the right to run a model; key permissions control whether a particular key may use that right. A key limited to selected models does not automatically gain access to a newly purchased model. A visible model catalog is not proof of active execution access. For Codex or Claude Code, the public guide instructs users to enable the key's Codex / Claude Code compatibility option. A minimal HTTP request Set RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY in your local environment using your preferred secret-handling mechanism, then run: Copy curl --fail-with-body https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"glm-5.3","messages":{"role":"user","content":"Reply with a short greeting."}}' The variable above is a placeholder for your local secret. Never place a real key in a public repository, screenshot, support message, or committed client configuration. Use the model catalog endpoint to check identifiers, then make a small request with a model your account and key can access. Coding clients and other applications The public connection guide covers OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Continue, Hermes, and other compatible clients. The dashboard provides automatic commands and manual setup examples for supported operating systems. Client configuration is version-specific. For example, the official guide distinguishes OpenCode v1 and v2 configuration formats. Prefer the current dashboard instructions over copying an old configuration block from a third-party article. The client contributes the editor or terminal interface, local tools, MCP connections, project instructions, and conversation management. Available model features depend on both the selected model and the integration. A compatible endpoint does not imply every feature of every first-party API is available. Troubleshooting without exposing secrets Check the base URL and exact model identifier, active subscription or trial, key model permissions, expiry, IP restrictions, and the compatibility option where required. If requests overlap, account for the shared slot pool. Keep the time and request identifier when contacting support, and remove authorization headers and private prompt content. title: Privacy, data handling, and availability
excerpt: Rate Cloud's public architecture distinguishes request content, temporary computation state, operational metadata, and account or payment records. These categories serve different purposes and ha
text: Rate Cloud's public architecture distinguishes request content, temporary computation state, operational metadata, and account or payment records. These categories serve different purposes and have different retention rules. This article summarizes the published policy and design rather than an independent security audit. Request content and temporary buffers The service states that it does not create a permanent history of prompt and response texts and does not train models on user data. Request content is processed in temporary memory. The documented cleanup targets for accessible, managed application buffers are up to five seconds after successful delivery and up to thirty seconds after a final error, cancellation, or disconnected connection. These application-buffer targets should not be generalized into a claim that every physical copy on every accelerator is provably erased within those exact times. The public architecture acknowledges a separate trust boundary for rented hardware. Isolated computational cache A computational KV cache has a separate lifetime: up to five minutes without reuse and a maximum absolute age of fifteen minutes. Expired entries become ineligible for new cache hits. An operation already using an entry may finish within its deadline; memory is cleared after the last reference is released. The documented cache is not persisted to disk or included in snapshots. Compatibility includes the account, model, weight revision, quantization, tokenizer, conversation template, and system instructions. The index is HMAC-protected, and a user cannot select another account's cache area. A project policy can specify a profile without cross-request caching. Client-side history is separate. An editor, agent, bot, or application may keep its own conversations and files according to its own settings. Operational metadata The public architecture describes metadata including identifiers, model and profile, timestamps, durations, usage, slot state, and error codes, with detailed records removed after thirty days. Those records exclude prompts, responses, tool arguments, files, and authorization tokens. Account, payment, and voluntarily submitted support information have separate purposes and retention rules. “No permanent prompt history” does not mean “no account or operational records.” Consult the current privacy policy linked from the website for the applicable legal details. Transport and infrastructure boundaries The architecture describes TLS for external transport, identity checks and mTLS between services, access on a service-need basis, and separation of keys, accounts, projects, and cache scopes. API secrets and request bodies are excluded from logs and backups under the documented rules. Protected transport and hardware-protected computation are different guarantees. The site does not promise confidential-computing protection on every accelerator. A node that loses trusted management is excluded, its authority is revoked, and its return requires verification and cleanup. Availability and interrupted work Continuous 24/7 availability of every model is not guaranteed. Recovery may retry an operation on a compatible replica before output begins, within the original deadline. It can add latency. Once a stream has begun, interruption must remain visible as an incomplete operation rather than a falsely completed response. The published compensation rule applies to a complete continuous system outage lasting more than four hours with HTTP 503 responses. It provides extensions of twelve hours for a three-day subscription, one day for a seven-day subscription, and three days for a thirty-day subscription. Individual model failures, slow responses, concurrency limits, and other error codes are not covered by that specific rule. The applicable terms and mandatory user rights remain controlling. When reporting an incident, provide the time and operation identifiers. Do not send API secrets or confidential request content. Source: Rate Cloud: data handling, security, and availability . Refer to the current terms and privacy policy linked from the official website . Snapshot: November 3, 2026. Back to overview .

text: Rate Cloud's White Label offering lets a partner sell model subscriptions under their own brand while Rate Cloud supplies and maintains the technical service. The partner focuses on branding, pricing, and customer acquisition. What the published offer includes The website describes a branded website and customer dashboard, a domain and hosting, payments, a partner panel, a Telegram bot, customer technical support, model infrastructure, updates, and fixes. Branding changes include the logo, colors, fonts, and other agreed design elements. The final scope is agreed before launch. The public page also presents application and assistant concepts. It explicitly identifies the illustrated interfaces as demonstrations based on OpenCode and describes shared applications with neutral branding. Those illustrations should not be interpreted as an independently verified release of a separate native app for every partner. Commercial model As published on November 3, 2026, setup costs $98.80 once, with no mandatory monthly maintenance fee. The USD setup amount is a dated display equivalent using the website's currency metadata on November 3, 2026; confirm the current price before purchase. Model subscriptions still have their base cost. Included maintenance does not make access to the models free. A partner adds a markup to the base Rate Cloud subscription price. text: Continue supports OpenAI-compatible models through its OpenAI provider and a custom apiBase . This guide uses Continue's current config.yaml format and stores the key in Continue's local secret-resolution file rather than in the YAML. Documentation checked: November 3, 2026. This is a static docs-based configuration, not a live request from Continue or a Rate Cloud account. Continue's current docs prefer YAML; config.json is deprecated. The pages checked do not state a minimum Continue client version for this configuration. If your version does not accept a field, follow the current schema linked below. Official references: Rate Cloud connection guide , Continue OpenAI-compatible model setup , Continue YAML reference , Continue secret FAQ , and Continue configuration locations . Check access and model IDs Create a Rate Cloud API key, allow the model you need, and make sure your account has an active trial or subscription for it. The key is displayed in full at creation time. Continue's model list does not grant access by itself. Rate Cloud's OpenAI-compatible base URL is https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 . Use the exact direct API IDs below. Continue displays the name you set in its picker; it does not require the ratecloud/ prefix used by some other clients. Model Direct API ID GLM 5.3 glm-5.3 GLM 5.3 Flash glm-5.3-flash DeepSeek V4.1 Flash deepseek-v4.1-flash DeepSeek V4 Pro deepseek-v4-pro Qwen 3.8 Max qwen-3.8-max Store the secret for the IDE extension Continue's IDE extensions resolve ${{ secrets.NAME }} from .env files. Its docs specify this lookup order: workspace .env , workspace .continue/.env , then global ~/.continue/.env . The docs warn that IDE extensions do not inherit shell environment variables directly. Create or update the global file ~/.continue/.env (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.continue\.env ) with this local entry: Copy RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY=<your-key> Keep this local file out of version control. Do not put a real key in config.yaml or share the .env file. For Continue CLI, the process environment can also resolve the secret, according to Continue's docs. Configure Continue's local YAML Continue stores its local config at ~/.continue/config.yaml on macOS/Linux and %USERPROFILE%\.continue\config.yaml on Windows. Use the config selector and gear icon in the Continue sidebar to open it. Preserve existing non-model sections. Add a model entry for each model you want to expose; this example includes all five: Copy name: Rate Cloud version: 1.0.0 schema: v1 models: - name: Rate Cloud - GLM 5.3 provider: openai model: glm-5.3 apiBase: https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 apiKey: ${{ secrets.RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY }} useResponsesApi: false roles: chat, edit, apply - name: Rate Cloud - GLM 5.3 Flash provider: openai model: glm-5.3-flash apiBase: https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 apiKey: ${{ secrets.RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY }} useResponsesApi: false roles: chat, edit, apply - name: Rate Cloud - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash provider: openai model: deepseek-v4.1-flash apiBase: https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 apiKey: ${{ secrets.RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY }} useResponsesApi: false roles: chat, edit, apply - name: Rate Cloud - DeepSeek V4 Pro provider: openai model: deepseek-v4-pro apiBase: https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 apiKey: ${{ secrets.RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY }} useResponsesApi: false roles: chat, edit, apply - name: Rate Cloud - Qwen 3.8 Max provider: openai model: qwen-3.8-max apiBase: https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 apiKey: ${{ secrets.RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY }} useResponsesApi: false roles: chat, edit, apply useResponsesApi: false selects the documented Chat Completions path. The models are listed with chat, edit, and apply roles. This guide does not assign an Agent/tool-use capability because that depends on actual model/API tool-call support; enable that capability only after verifying it for the model you use. Save the config. Continue's current configuration guide says it automatically reloads changes. Select a Rate Cloud entry from the model picker. No model request is necessary just to check the static config and picker entry. Troubleshooting API key resolves as missing: check the exact RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY spelling and that the key is in a supported .env location. For IDE extensions, do not rely only on an export in a terminal. No Rate Cloud model appears: confirm the YAML is at the local config path, schema: v1 is present, and the saved file remains valid YAML. Use the Continue config selector to confirm you are editing the active config. 401 or access denied: check that the secret is active and that Rate Cloud allows the selected model for both the key and account. A model name appearing in Continue does not prove access. 404 or wrong API route: keep apiBase at https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 ; do not append /chat/completions to the base URL. Agent tool calls fail: roles and endpoint tool-call support are separate. Continue documents tool_use as required for Agent mode, but actual Rate Cloud compatibility has not been live-tested here. Do not declare it unless verified. Config shape differs in your release: Continue's reference is the owner for supported YAML fields. Prefer config.yaml ; JSON configs are documented as deprecated. Remove secrets and private prompt content from logs before sharing diagnostics. No installs or API requests were run while preparing this guide. Russian version: Подключение Continue к Rate Cloud . text: Rate Cloud provides an OpenAI-compatible API for clients that allow a custom base URL, and a standard-library Python example for direct calls. These examples do not install packages and do not make a request until you choose to run them. Official reference: Rate Cloud API and connection documentation . Endpoints Purpose Method and URL OpenAI-compatible base URL https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 List models GET https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/models Chat completions POST https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/chat/completions Responses API POST https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/responses For /v1 requests, send Authorization: Bearer <API key> . Use a model ID exactly as shown in the table: Model Direct API ID GLM 5.3 glm-5.3 GLM 5.3 Flash glm-5.3-flash DeepSeek V4.1 Flash deepseek-v4.1-flash DeepSeek V4 Pro deepseek-v4-pro Qwen 3.8 Max qwen-3.8-max Do not add a provider prefix such as ratecloud/ to a direct HTTP model ID. The ratecloud/ and ocx-claude-ratecloud-- forms are for particular client integrations. Set an environment variable On macOS or Linux, use the block for your shell. Both variants read the secret without echoing it. The variable is removed when you run unset or close the terminal. Copy Bash read -r -s -p 'Rate Cloud API key: ' RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY printf '\n' export RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY Copy zsh (the default macOS shell) read -r -s 'RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY?Rate Cloud API key: ' printf '\n' export RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY On Windows PowerShell, set $env:RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY in the session that runs your client. Do not put a real key in source code, a committed .env file, or a public issue. Optional connectivity check with curl This sends a simple request to the model catalog. It confirms that the endpoint responds and the key is accepted, but does not prove that a specific model is subscribed or permitted for the key. Copy curl --fail-with-body 'https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1/models' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY" Python 3 standard-library example Save this as a local .py file. It uses only Python's standard library ( urllib.request ), reads the secret from the environment, and sends one small chat-completions request when you run it. Change MODEL to another exact direct API ID if desired. Copy import json import os import sys from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError from urllib.request import Request, urlopen BASE_URL = "https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1" MODEL = "glm-5.3" API_KEY = os.environ.get("RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY") if not API_KEY: sys.exit("Set RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY in the environment before running this script.") payload = { "model": MODEL, "messages": {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with a short greeting."} , } request = Request( f"{BASE_URL}/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"), headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json", }, method="POST", ) try: with urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response: result = json.load(response) print(result"choices"0"message""content") except HTTPError as error: Avoid printing request headers or the API key in diagnostics. print(f"HTTP error: {error.code} {error.reason}", file=sys.stderr) sys.exit(1) except URLError as error: print(f"Connection error: {error.reason}", file=sys.stderr) sys.exit(1) except (KeyError, IndexError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error: print(f"Unexpected response format: {error}", file=sys.stderr) sys.exit(1) Run it from the shell where RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY is set. Do not print the full response in shared logs if prompts or model outputs may contain private information. Troubleshooting 401 or authentication error: confirm the environment variable is set in the process environment, the key is active and unexpired, and the Authorization header uses Bearer followed by the key. 403 or access denied: verify trial or subscription access for the requested model, key model permissions, IP restrictions, and any client compatibility flag required by a dedicated client endpoint. 404 or model not found: check the endpoint path and exact model spelling. Use /v1 for these generic examples, not the Codex or Claude Code compatibility endpoints. The catalog lists a model but generation is denied: the catalog is not proof of account or key permission. Confirm both model subscription and key access in the dashboard. Timeout or incomplete output: retry only after checking the response state. A timeout does not establish that the operation completed; avoid blindly repeating requests that trigger costly side effects in your own application. When asking support for help, share the time, model ID, endpoint path, HTTP status, and request identifier if available. Remove API keys, authorization headers, and private prompt or response content.

text: OpenClaw can register a custom provider with an OpenAI-compatible base URL. This guide uses its documented openai-completions transport and Rate Cloud's OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. Documentation checked: November 3, 2026. This is a static configuration example based on the published docs. It has not been live-tested against an OpenClaw installation or Rate Cloud account. OpenClaw docs are rolling docs and do not specify a minimum supported app version here; use the current config format for your installed version. Official references: Rate Cloud connection guide , Rate Cloud's OpenClaw example , OpenClaw custom providers , OpenClaw provider examples , OpenClaw environment variables , and OpenClaw secret references . Requirements and access Create a Rate Cloud API key in the dashboard. Allow the model you want to use, confirm a trial or active subscription for it, and copy the full secret at creation time. A model catalog listing does not itself grant execution access. Rate Cloud documents this endpoint for OpenAI-compatible requests: Copy https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1 Select the openai-completions adapter. Do not add /chat/completions to the base URL. Rate Cloud's direct model IDs are: Model Direct API ID OpenClaw model reference GLM 5.3 glm-5.3 ratecloud/glm-5.3 GLM 5.3 Flash glm-5.3-flash ratecloud/glm-5.3-flash DeepSeek V4.1 Flash deepseek-v4.1-flash ratecloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash DeepSeek V4 Pro deepseek-v4-pro ratecloud/deepseek-v4-pro Qwen 3.8 Max qwen-3.8-max ratecloud/qwen-3.8-max The OpenClaw model reference includes the provider ID; the request sent upstream uses the bare model ID. Supply the key without putting it in the config OpenClaw supports ${VARIABLE_NAME} substitution in provider apiKey values. The current OpenClaw docs recommend the global ~/.openclaw/.env file for provider keys, which is also read when a Gateway runs as a service. Add this local entry (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.openclaw\.env ): Copy RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY=<your-key> Keep this file local and restrict access to it. OpenClaw's dotenv loader does not expand references inside .env values, so put the actual key on the right side of the assignment. Do not put the literal key in a shared openclaw.json , source repository, or public issue. Restart the Gateway if its current process has not loaded the new environment value. Add the custom provider Open the existing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json on macOS/Linux or %USERPROFILE%\.openclaw\openclaw.json on Windows. Back it up, then merge the models and agents fields below with the existing configuration. Do not replace unrelated settings. The object is JSON5 in OpenClaw, so this no-comment sample is also valid JSON. Copy { "models": { "mode": "merge", "providers": { "ratecloud": { "baseUrl": "https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1", "apiKey": "${RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY}", "api": "openai-completions", "models": { "id": "glm-5.3", "name": "GLM 5.3" }, { "id": "glm-5.3-flash", "name": "GLM 5.3 Flash" }, { "id": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "name": "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash" }, { "id": "deepseek-v4-pro", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Pro" }, { "id": "qwen-3.8-max", "name": "Qwen 3.8 Max" } } } }, "agents": { "defaults": { "model": { "primary": "ratecloud/glm-5.3" } } } } This example uses the fields in the current OpenClaw custom provider docs and the Rate Cloud example: baseUrl , apiKey , api , models , and agents.defaults.model.primary . It does not assert context length, image support, tool compatibility, or reasoning behavior. Leave those unspecified unless you have verified them for the endpoint and model. Select and troubleshoot Restart the Gateway after saving the config, then choose the configured Rate Cloud model. For a static check, confirm that the primary model reference exactly matches a provider/model ID in the config. Do not use a live model-list or generation command unless you intend to make an authenticated API request. Provider/model is unknown: check that models.providers.ratecloud.models has the exact bare ID and that the selected reference is ratecloud/<same-id> . Unauthorized: confirm the Gateway process can read RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY , that the key is active, and that its IP restrictions allow the Gateway host. Access denied: check key model permissions and trial/subscription access for that specific model. Tool calls or images fail: the generic protocol does not guarantee every feature. Do not add reasoning , input , contextWindow , or compatibility overrides unless the actual endpoint/model supports them. Using older OpenClaw configuration: the docs may evolve. Check the current custom provider reference rather than copying a legacy models.json schema into openclaw.json . Remove credentials and private prompts before sharing diagnostics. text: This guide configures OpenCode to use Rate Cloud's OpenAI-compatible API. It covers the documented OpenCode v1 configuration format. Rate Cloud's live connection page distinguishes v1 and v2 formats; for v2, use the current v2 example in the dashboard rather than pasting a v1 configuration into it. Official references: Rate Cloud connection guide and OpenCode configuration . Before you start Sign in to Rate Cloud and create an API key in Settings → API keys . Copy it when created because the full secret is shown only once. Ensure the key allows the model you intend to use and that you have an active trial or subscription for that model. The model list can show models without granting execution access. OpenCode's v1 provider configuration uses the ratecloud/ prefix when selecting the configured provider. This prefix is for the client. The model ID sent through the direct HTTP API does not include it. The exact direct API IDs are: Model Direct API ID OpenCode v1 selection GLM 5.3 glm-5.3 ratecloud/glm-5.3 GLM 5.3 Flash glm-5.3-flash ratecloud/glm-5.3-flash DeepSeek V4.1 Flash deepseek-v4.1-flash ratecloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash DeepSeek V4 Pro deepseek-v4-pro ratecloud/deepseek-v4-pro Qwen 3.8 Max qwen-3.8-max ratecloud/qwen-3.8-max Set the key in your shell The examples below read the key without echoing it. Use the block for your shell: Bash, or zsh (the default macOS shell). Enter the secret at the prompt. The variable is available to programs launched from that shell; close the terminal when finished or remove it with unset . Copy Bash read -r -s -p 'Rate Cloud API key: ' RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY printf '\n' export RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY Copy zsh read -r -s 'RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY?Rate Cloud API key: ' printf '\n' export RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY Do not paste the key into a shared config file, source repository, screenshot, or support message. On Windows, set RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY in the environment used to launch OpenCode, using your usual secure local secret-handling method. Configure OpenCode v1 Open the existing OpenCode configuration at ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json on macOS/Linux. Preserve other providers and settings. Merge the provider entry below into your existing object, then set or merge the top-level model value. If the file is new, this complete minimal example selects GLM 5.3: Copy { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "model": "ratecloud/glm-5.3", "provider": { "ratecloud": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "name": "Rate Cloud", "options": { "baseURL": "https://llm.rate-cloud.com/v1", "apiKey": "{env:RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY}" }, "models": { "glm-5.3": { "name": "GLM 5.3" }, "glm-5.3-flash": { "name": "GLM 5.3 Flash" }, "deepseek-v4.1-flash": { "name": "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash" }, "deepseek-v4-pro": { "name": "DeepSeek V4 Pro" }, "qwen-3.8-max": { "name": "Qwen 3.8 Max" } } } } } OpenCode substitutes {env:RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY} from the environment when it loads the config. An unset variable becomes an empty string, so export the key before launching OpenCode. The config stores only the variable reference, not the secret. On Windows, the documented user config location is %USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json . OpenCode v1 and v2 use different provider structures. For OpenCode v2, follow the v2-specific manual example in the Rate Cloud dashboard; do not convert this v1 sample by guesswork. Select a model and check the connection Restart OpenCode after changing its config, open the model picker ( /models in the TUI), and select a Rate Cloud model. Start with a short non-sensitive request. Use the matching ID from the OpenCode v1 selection column above. Troubleshooting Rate Cloud is missing from the model list: confirm the config was saved in the location for your OS and that the JSON is valid. Check that provider.ratecloud and the selected model are merged at the correct top level. The request is unauthorized or denied: make sure RATE_CLOUD_API_KEY was exported in the same shell that launched OpenCode. Check key expiry, IP restrictions, model permissions, and trial or subscription access in the dashboard. The key appears blank: OpenCode replaces an unset environment variable with an empty value. Set it before launching the client, then restart OpenCode. A request is rejected for the model: use the exact lowercase ID, including punctuation, and ensure the key and account can run that model. A visible catalog entry alone is not proof of access. You use OpenCode v2: use its own providers format from the dashboard. Do not insert this v1 provider example into a v2 file. When contacting support, share the client version, operating system, model ID, time, and error text after removing API keys, authorization headers, and private prompt content.
